title: Interpretable distillation reveals that deep learning splicing models suffer from pervasive confounders and blind spots.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed 4 GitHub LFS (large file storage) files. Liao_2023_SplicingPredictions.csv.gz (42 MB): 239,772 rows, 37 columns, unique 70-nt exon sequences, measured PSI (fraction of reads including the exon) with raw read counts (median 168 reads), no missing values; PSI is bimodal (16% exactly 0, 6% exactly 1, median 0.90). Same table holds SpliceAI, Pangolin and AlphaGenome scores; I computed their Pearson correlation with PSI as 0.846, 0.805 and 0.841. Chong_2019 (MFASS, 31,031 rows: 27,733 mutant, 2,339 natural, 959 control; hg19/hg38 coordinates and Ensembl exon IDs). Baeza_Centurion_2025: 5,976 indel/substitution variants with psi on a 0–100 scale. Zenodo listing: one 587 MB zip.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That PSI in the Liao library was measured by RNA-seq in a reporter with fixed flanking context; that MFASS inclusion comes from fluorescence sorting; the published per-assay correlations (Liao 0.83–0.86, FAS exon 6 0.81–0.88, MFASS 0.37–0.44). I did not open the GEO raw data or the FAS exon 6 table (not in repo listing), and did not check the Liao 2023 PNAS model's reported score.

a1_downloadable.note: Public GitHub LFS files and Zenodo, no login; verified by download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Measured PSI is a column ('PSI' in Liao table, 'psi' in Baeza-Centurion, 'v2_index'/'v1_index' in MFASS); verified in files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Full exon sequences present as strings in every table; flanking reporter context is in Lib2.gbk in the repo (not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: PSI is a fraction 0–1 in Liao/MFASS and a percentage 0–100 in Baeza-Centurion (seen in files); the scale differs across tables and must be rescaled.

a5_enough_rows.note: 239,772 labelled synthetic exons, plus 31,031 MFASS and 5,976 indel rows for transfer tests; counted in files.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~60 MB compressed, a few hundred MB in pandas
a6_fits_laptop.note: Loaded all three tables in pandas on the laptop without trouble.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: MFASS 27,733 variants matches the Chong 2018 abstract; paper's '16,469 MFASS sequences' is a filtered subset of the 31,031-row file, not checked exactly. Liao count not stated in the text I read.

a8_label_provenance.note: PSI comes from RNA-seq read counts in a reporter assay (counts present as columns), not from a model. The deep-model score columns and distillation_test.csv are model outputs and must be used only as features/baselines, never as labels.

B1.why: One 239,772-row table with sequence, label and three baseline-model scores; seen in file.

B2.why: gzip CSV parsed with pandas on first try, zero missing values in Liao table.

B3.why: Within Liao one assay; across tables PSI scales differ (0–1 vs 0–100) and MFASS uses fluorescence.

B4.why: No censoring markers, but 22% of PSI sits exactly at 0 or 1 (floor/ceiling), seen in file.

B5.why: Zero duplicate exon sequences in Liao table, checked.

B6.why: data/README cites sources; column meanings mostly self-explanatory but no data dictionary.

C1.why: Transfer synthetic→natural exons is informative either way; in-library accuracy alone needs to beat Liao 2023.

C2.why: Liao 2023 PNAS open interpretable model on same library, plus this paper's open distilled models and SpliceAI/Pangolin/AlphaGenome.

C3.why: Weak 'better' angle: deep models miss RNA structure and CpG confounders named here; fixing them is the hook.

C4.why: Splicing reporter assays are lab-based, but deep-model predictions are already cheap.

C5.why: Published correlations 0.83–0.86 (Liao) and 0.37–0.44 (MFASS); score columns already in files.

D1.why: RNA-FM and Nucleotide Transformer are open-weight; SpliceAI/Pangolin open too.

D2.why: 70-nt exons plus flanks: embeddings for 240k sequences cacheable on CPU in hours.

D3.why: Repo GPLv3; SpliceAI scores under its own licence and AlphaGenome outputs non-commercial terms.

E1.why: Hold out whole assays (train Liao, test MFASS/Baeza-Centurion), or sequence-cluster splits within Liao.

E2.why: Three independent assays plus 2,198 MFASS exon backgrounds as groups.

E3.why: Global mean PSI and existing deep-model scores are ready-made baselines.

E4.why: Read counts per exon give binomial noise; MFASS has R1/R2 replicate columns.

E5.why: Splice-site strength (MaxEnt-style scores) and GC/hexamer effects known to drive inclusion must be recovered.

E6.why: Label shuffling and feature-block ablation (sequence vs structure vs model scores) straightforward.

E7.why: MFASS (Chong 2018) and Baeza-Centurion 2025 indels are independent labs and assays, in repo.

E8.why: Paper's per-assay correlations recomputable from provided columns; I got 0.846 for SpliceAI on Liao.

G1.why: MFASS has Ensembl exon IDs and hg38 coordinates; Liao library is synthetic (no IDs).

G2.why: Vex-seq/MaPSy splicing MPRAs and SpliceVarDB plausible, joinable only via coordinates for natural exons.

G3.why: Coordinate joins workable for MFASS; synthetic exons do not join to anything.

G4.why: Combining MPRAs asks whether synthetic-exon training improves natural-variant prediction; modest beyond what exists.

H1.why: Full PSI range including 16% fully skipped exons; negatives systematically measured.

H2.why: Three assays, but each one cell line and one reporter context; Liao exons are random synthetic.

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below: inclusion of short exons in fixed reporter context, in one cell type.

H4.why: Paper discusses non-reference blind spots; reporter-context limits only partly explicit.

I1.why: Splicing-model developers and clinical variant-interpretation groups; no specific adopter named.

I2.why: Could change which splicing score is trusted for exonic variants; marginal unless transfer gain large.

I3.why: Correlation with PSI roughly matches; clinical use needs a splice-disrupting yes/no threshold.

I4.why: Paper shows additive motif models explain much, but structure interactions are genuinely nonlinear.

J1.why: Real modelling: embeddings, cross-assay transfer, ablations, calibration.

J2.why: PSI and splice-site logic are interpretable, but MPRA artifacts need domain judgement.

J3.why: A cross-assay benchmark of existing scores is shareable even before any new model.

existing_models.name: Liao, Sudarshan & Regev 2023 PNAS interpretable-by-design splicing network
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained and tested on this same synthetic exon library (GSE200096); exact held-out score not retrieved.

existing_models.name: Interpretable distillation models (this paper; SpliceAI/Pangolin/AlphaGenome distilled)
existing_models.score_and_split: Distil deep-model predictions, not measured PSI; deep models score Pearson 0.83–0.86 on Liao, 0.37–0.44 on MFASS.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Deep models exploit CpG and stop-codon confounders and are blind to RNA structure, failing on non-reference sequences.

existing_models.name: SpliceAI, Pangolin, AlphaGenome (genome-trained deep models)
existing_models.score_and_split: Scores precomputed in the files; my recomputed Pearson with Liao PSI: 0.846, 0.805, 0.841 (zero-shot).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Per this paper: RNA structure and genomic confounders.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (RNA language model) or Nucleotide Transformer embeddings, plus precomputed SpliceAI/Pangolin scores as features
backbone.licence: RNA-FM open code/weights; repo GPLv3; AlphaGenome outputs non-commercial terms

integration.partner_dataset: MFASS (Chong 2018) and Baeza-Centurion 2025 indel MPRA, both in repo; Vex-seq/MaPSy as further MPRAs
integration.join_key: hg38 coordinates / Ensembl exon ID (natural exons only)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does training on 240k measured synthetic exons fix the structure blind spots of genome-trained splicing models well enough to improve prediction on natural human exon variants?

controls.positive_control: Recover splice-site strength and known exonic splicing enhancer/silencer hexamer effects; reproduce SpliceAI Pearson 0.846 on Liao from provided columns.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle PSI labels (must collapse to mean); ablate structure features; random-noise features.
controls.external_validation: Train on Liao synthetic library, test on MFASS natural exons and Baeza-Centurion indels (different labs and assays).

honest_claim_h3: Predicts inclusion of short (70-nt) exons in a fixed reporter context in one cell line, and tests whether that transfers to other reporter assays of natural exons — not endogenous, tissue-specific splicing.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use exon DNA sequence, its predicted RNA folding and existing splicing-model scores to predict how often the exon is kept in mRNA.
plain_idea.train_on: 239,772 synthetic 70-letter exon sequences (verified), each with folding energy and three existing models' scores.
plain_idea.predict: The fraction of RNA molecules that include the exon (PSI), measured by sequencing a reporter construct in cells; tested on two other labs' reporter assays.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups interpreting splicing variants would learn whether lab-measured synthetic data fixes known blind spots of genome-trained models; a failure to transfer is itself a useful benchmark result.

more_or_better_data.why: Same 239,772-exon library Liao 2023 already trained on, so not more data for that model; but SpliceAI/Pangolin never saw measured PSI on non-reference sequences.

confidence_score.why: Per-exon read counts (median 168) allow binomial uncertainty, and MFASS has replicates; SpliceAI/Pangolin give no calibrated PSI uncertainty, Liao 2023 not checked.

models_beatable.why: Genome-trained models reach only 0.37–0.44 on MFASS (paper); Liao 2023 is a recent purpose-built model on this exact library, likely hard to beat in-library.

guaranteed_improvement.why: MFASS and Baeza-Centurion measure inclusion with different reporters and readouts (fluorescence vs RNA-seq), so the same-quantity-same-way condition fails.

label_elsewhere.sources: Other splicing MPRAs (MFASS, Baeza-Centurion in repo; Vex-seq, MaPSy known resources); endogenous PSI in GTEx/VastDB (known resources, different context)
label_elsewhere.why: Several independent reporter assays allow cross-assay external validation, though labels are not directly comparable.

ambitious.why: Publishes splicing-model benchmarks; would need a structure-aware model that clearly lifts MFASS correlation over SpliceAI's ~0.4.

realistic.why: Fits a cross-assay benchmark showing how far synthetic-MPRA training transfers to natural exons.

fallback.why: A negative transfer result with honest ablations is still a publishable benchmark note.

pitch.headline: 239,772 measured synthetic exons in one 42 MB table, with SpliceAI, Pangolin and AlphaGenome scores already alongside every row.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Random non-genomic exons, so no genomic confounders; zero duplicates, zero missing values, read counts per exon (median 168) for noise estimates; two independent assays (31,031 and 5,976 rows) ship in the same repo.
pitch.the_win: A model trained on synthetic exons that beats the genome-trained models' 0.37–0.44 Pearson on MFASS natural exons.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: Quantifies how much synthetic-library training transfers across reporter assays, and whether structure features add anything beyond existing scores.
pitch.who_wants_it: Splicing-model developers (Regev lab, Pangolin/SpliceAI authors) and clinical variant-interpretation groups choosing splice scores for exonic variants.

ml_idea: Train a head on frozen RNA-FM embeddings + RNA folding features + existing deep-model scores to predict measured PSI on the Liao synthetic library, then evaluate zero-shot on MFASS and Baeza-Centurion to test whether measured synthetic data corrects the structure/confounder blind spots named in this paper.

effort.compute_note: Estimated: 240k short sequences at roughly 30–50 per second for RNA-FM on CPU; loading timed informally (seconds).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Retrieve Liao 2023 PNAS's held-out score and whether it was already tested on MFASS; if it already transfers well, the project is a re-run.

verdict_reason: Model-ready 240k-row measured PSI table, but Liao 2023 PNAS already modelled this exact library; only the cross-assay transfer angle is open, so check what Liao 2023 reported first.
